alabama.hold: Up to 7 days from the first day of confinement.
alabama.initiators: A law enforcement officer, working with a community mental health officer, takes the person into custody. Any person can also ask the probate court to commit someone by filing a petition.
alabama.link_label: Alabama Department of Mental Health — Involuntary Commitment

alaska.initiators: A peace officer, a psychiatrist or physician licensed in Alaska or employed by the federal government, or a licensed clinical psychologist who has probable cause to believe the person is gravely disabled or mentally ill and likely to cause serious harm.
alaska.hearing: Unless the person is released or agrees to stay voluntarily within 72 hours, the person is entitled to a court hearing set for no later than the end of that 72-hour period.

arizona.hold: Up to 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, unless a petition for a court-ordered evaluation is filed.
arizona.initiators: Any responsible person who knows the facts — a relative, a friend, a peace officer, or the admitting officer — can apply in writing for emergency admission.
arizona.link_label: Arizona Revised Statutes § 36-527 — Discharge and release

arkansas.hold: Up to 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
arkansas.initiators: Any person who has reason to believe someone meets the standard can file a verified petition with the court, and a peace officer can take the person into custody in an emergency.

california.hold: Up to 72 hours for assessment, evaluation, and crisis intervention.
california.hold_extra: If the person still meets the standard after 72 hours, the facility can certify them for up to 14 more days of intensive treatment (a “5250”).
california.initiators: A peace officer, a professional in charge of a county-designated evaluation facility, a member of the attending staff, a designated member of a mobile crisis team, or a professional designated by the county — on probable cause that the person is a danger to self or others, or gravely disabled.
california.hearing: If the person is certified for 14 more days, a certification review hearing must be held within 4 days of the certification. If the person is not certified and is still held on the 5150, a review hearing must be held within 7 days of the first detention.
california.link_label: California Legislative Information — Welfare and Institutions Code § 5150

colorado.initiators: A certified peace officer, a clinician (called an “intervening professional”), or a judge acting on a sworn affidavit. Any person with a personal connection to the individual can also petition the court for an emergency hold.

connecticut.hold: 72 hours for examination. If a physician then signs an emergency certificate, the person can be confined for up to 15 days without a court order.
connecticut.hold_extra: A psychiatrist must examine the person within 24 hours of admission; if the psychiatrist finds the person does not meet the standard, the person must be released.
connecticut.initiators: A physician can sign the emergency certificate. Police officers and others can bring the person to a hospital for the 72-hour examination.
connecticut.hearing: If a commitment application is filed in probate court before the 15 days run out, the emergency certificate can continue for another 15 days or until the court case finishes.
connecticut.link_label: Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services — Physician's Certificate

delaware.hold: Up to 24 hours in a designated psychiatric facility.
delaware.hold_extra: A separate 48-hour provisional admission can follow if the criteria are still met.
delaware.initiators: A peace officer or a credentialed mental health screener completes the request for emergency detention. Any person who believes someone is dangerous because of a mental condition can notify a peace officer or a screener.
delaware.link_label: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services — 24-Hour Emergency Detention Form

florida.hold: Up to 72 hours for involuntary examination at a receiving facility, starting when the person arrives.
florida.initiators: A law enforcement officer, a physician, a clinical psychologist, a psychiatric nurse, or a judge by ex parte order.
florida.hearing: If the facility files a petition for involuntary placement, the court must hold a hearing within 5 court working days, and must appoint the public defender within 1 court working day if the person has no lawyer.

georgia.initiators: A physician can sign a certificate after examining the person, and a peace officer can take the person to a physician or an emergency receiving facility.

hawaii.hold: The person must be released within 72 hours of admission unless the person agrees to stay voluntarily or a court proceeding is started.
hawaii.hold_extra: A police officer first calls mental health emergency workers, and an emergency examination decides whether the criteria for hospitalization are met.
hawaii.initiators: A police officer who believes a person is imminently dangerous to self or others, or gravely disabled, calls for help from mental health emergency workers designated by the director. A physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or advanced practice nurse performs the emergency examination.
hawaii.link_label: Hawaii Revised Statutes § 334-46 — Emergency hospitalization (Hawaii State Legislature)

idaho.hold_extra: The evidence must be put before a court within 24 hours. If the court finds grave disability or imminent danger, it orders a temporary custody order and an examination.
idaho.initiators: A peace officer can take the person into custody, or a physician, physician assistant, or advanced practice registered nurse at a hospital can detain a person already there.
idaho.hearing: A hearing must be held within 5 days of the detention order.
idaho.link_label: Idaho Code § 66-326 — Detention without hearing (Idaho Legislature)

illinois.initiators: Any person 18 or older can present a petition to the director of a mental health facility when immediate hospitalization is needed, and a peace officer can take the person into custody.

indiana.hold: Up to 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
indiana.hold_extra: The facility must file its application for emergency detention within 48 hours of admission. If the court authorizes detention, the person may not be held more than 14 days from admission, not counting weekends and holidays, while waiting for a final hearing.
indiana.initiators: A facility files an application for emergency detention, with a physician’s statement that there is probable cause to believe the person is mentally ill and dangerous or gravely disabled.
indiana.hearing: If the court authorizes detention, a final hearing follows — the person cannot be held more than 14 days (not counting weekends and holidays) waiting for it.
indiana.link_label: Application for Emergency Detention — Indiana Code 12-26-5 (Indiana Courts)

iowa.hold: Up to 48 hours from the date of the magistrate’s order, not counting Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.
iowa.initiators: A judge can order immediate custody, and a peace officer can take the person to the nearest facility without a warrant when there is no way to reach the court in time.
iowa.link_label: Iowa Code § 229.22 — Hospitalization, emergency procedure (Iowa Legislature)

kansas.hold: Kansas law sets no single maximum number of hours for an emergency hold. At a crisis intervention center, the person must be evaluated within 4 hours, a court must review the case within 48 hours, and the person must be discharged within 72 hours unless a petition for involuntary commitment is filed.
kansas.initiators: A law enforcement officer can take the person into custody without a warrant, and an application for emergency detention can be made to a treatment facility.
kansas.hearing: A district court reviews the case within 48 hours of admission to a crisis intervention center.
kansas.link_label: K.S.A. 59-29c08 — Evaluation, district court review and discharge (Kansas Legislature)

kentucky.hold: Up to 72 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, on a physician’s emergency admission.
kentucky.hold_extra: A peace officer can hold the person for up to 18 hours while an evaluation is done and the next step is arranged.
kentucky.initiators: A peace officer can take the person into custody and bring them to a hospital for evaluation, and an authorized staff physician can order a 72-hour emergency admission. A judge can also order hospitalization.
kentucky.link_label: KRS 202A.041 — Emergency admission by law enforcement (Kentucky Legislature)

louisiana.hold: Up to 15 days under an emergency certificate.
louisiana.hold_extra: Within 72 hours of admission, the coroner or a deputy must independently examine the person — that examination is required before the person can be held longer.
louisiana.initiators: A physician, physician assistant, psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner, certain other nurse practitioners, or a psychologist can sign an emergency certificate, but only after actually examining the person. A peace officer can take a person into protective custody, and a judge can order custody.
louisiana.hearing: The person or their lawyer can demand a hearing on whether there is probable cause to keep holding them, and the hearing must be held within 5 days of filing that demand.
louisiana.link_label: La. R.S. 28:53 — Admission by emergency certificate (Louisiana Legislature)

maine.hold: Up to 24 hours, while a judge reviews the application and certificate.
maine.hold_extra: If a second opinion does not certify the findings within 24 hours of admission, the person must be discharged immediately.
maine.initiators: Any health officer, law enforcement officer, or other person can apply for emergency admission, with a certificate signed by a medical practitioner who has examined the person. A law enforcement officer can take a person into protective custody.
maine.hearing: A judge reviews the application and certificate within the 24-hour window.

maryland.hold: Up to 30 hours in an emergency facility.
maryland.hold_extra: A physician must evaluate the person within 6 hours of arriving at the emergency facility.
maryland.initiators: A physician or other listed clinician who has examined the person, a peace or law enforcement officer who has personally observed the person, or any other interested person can file a petition for emergency evaluation.
maryland.hearing: A person who is involuntarily admitted gets a hearing before an administrative law judge within 10 days of admission.

massachusetts.initiators: A licensed physician, psychiatric nurse mental health clinical specialist, psychologist, or independent clinical social worker who examines the person can apply. A police officer can apply in an emergency when none of those professionals is available, and any person can ask the District Court to order commitment for up to 3 days.
massachusetts.hearing: The court must appoint a lawyer for the person, and a person admitted under Section 12(b) can ask for an emergency hearing.
massachusetts.link_label: Standards of Judicial Practice: Civil Commitment and Authorization of Medical Treatment fo

michigan.initiators: A peace officer who reasonably believes a person needs treatment and presents a serious danger can take the person into protective custody and bring them to a hospital. A court can also order hospitalization.
michigan.hearing: A hearing must be held within 7 days.

minnesota.hold: Up to 72 hours, not counting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.
minnesota.hold_extra: Every person held must be told in writing when admitted that they can leave after 72 hours, that they can have a medical examination within 48 hours, and that they can ask to change to voluntary status. The facility must release the person when the hold expires unless a court order is obtained, and a second emergency hold cannot be placed right after the first.
minnesota.initiators: An examiner’s written statement, with the head of the treatment facility’s consent, admits the person for emergency care. A peace officer or health officer can also take a person into custody and bring them to a physician or treatment facility.
minnesota.hearing: The hearing on a commitment petition must be held within 14 days of the petition being filed. If a judicial hold runs longer than 72 hours, the court must hold a preliminary hearing first.
minnesota.link_label: Minnesota Revisor of Statutes — Minn. Stat. § 253B.051, Emergency Admission

mississippi.initiators: A designated professional who has reason to believe the person is an immediate danger or gravely disabled can hold or admit the person. Any citizen can also start the process by filing a sworn statement at the chancery clerk’s office.
mississippi.hearing: The evaluation must be finished within 24 hours of the person being taken into custody, and after that the court orders a hearing within 7 to 10 days.

missouri.hold: Up to 96 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
missouri.initiators: A court can order detention when it finds probable cause, and a mental health coordinator or a peace officer can start an emergency evaluation when the danger is imminent.
missouri.hearing: The facility must release the person before the 96 hours run out unless it starts a court hearing for up to 21 more days of treatment.
missouri.link_label: Frequently Asked Questions | Missouri Department of Mental Health

montana.hold_extra: A mental health professional must evaluate the person within the first 24 hours of the hold, and the county attorney and the public defender’s office must be told right away.
montana.initiators: A mental health professional can place the person on the hold by written request, and a peace officer can take a person into custody in an emergency until a professional person can evaluate them.
montana.link_label: 53-21-154. 72-hour mental health hold, MCA - Montana Code Annotated 2025

nebraska.hold: There is no fixed maximum number of hours in the law. The person must be evaluated by a mental health professional as soon as reasonably possible, and no later than 36 hours after admission — and must be released after that evaluation unless the professional finds the person is mentally ill and dangerous.
nebraska.initiators: A law enforcement officer with probable cause can take the person into emergency protective custody, and a mental health professional with probable cause can hold the person until an officer arrives.
nebraska.hearing: If the professional finds the person is mentally ill and dangerous, the case goes to the mental health board for a hearing.

nevada.initiators: A designated person — such as a peace officer or physician — can take the person into custody for emergency admission, with a certificate from a psychiatrist or licensed psychologist (or a physician if neither is available).
nevada.link_label: Mental Health Crisis Holds - State of Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health

new-hampshire.hold: Up to 10 days, not counting Saturdays and Sundays.
new-hampshire.initiators: A petitioner or a law enforcement officer can sign a sworn complaint before a justice of the peace, and a peace officer can place a person in protective custody when the danger is immediate.
new-hampshire.hearing: A probable cause hearing must be held within 3 days of the admission, not counting Sundays and holidays.
new-hampshire.link_label: Chapter 135-C New Hampshire Mental Health Services System - New Hampshire General Court

new-jersey.hold: A screening service can hold the person for up to 24 hours for assessment. After that, the facility has up to 72 hours from the screening certificate to get a temporary court order — if it does not, the person must be released.
new-jersey.initiators: A state or local law enforcement officer takes the person to a screening service, a mental health screener can ask for that after an outreach visit, a court can order it, or an outpatient treatment provider can certify the need.
new-jersey.hearing: A full court hearing must take place within 20 days.
new-jersey.link_label: Directive #06-25 - Civil Commitments - Revised Protocol for Applications Pursuant to N.J.S

new-mexico.hold: The law sets no fixed number of hours. The person must be taken to an evaluation facility immediately — a jail can be used only in an extreme emergency, and for no more than 24 hours.
new-mexico.initiators: A peace officer can detain and transport the person, and a licensed physician, certified psychologist, or qualified mental health professional can certify that immediate detention is needed.
new-mexico.hearing: Every person admitted has the right to a hearing within 7 days of admission, and to a lawyer.
new-mexico.link_label: New Mexico Statutes, Chapter 43, Article 1 — Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities

new-york.hold_extra: A second physician on the hospital’s psychiatric staff must confirm the finding within 48 hours — if they disagree, the person must be released or offered voluntary admission.
new-york.initiators: The director of an approved hospital admits the person on a staff physician’s finding. Police and peace officers can bring a person to the hospital for emergency admission.
new-york.hearing: The person, or someone acting for them, can ask a court to review the admission, and the court can authorize retention for up to 15 days from admission.

north-carolina.hold: The person can be taken straight to a facility for examination, and held for up to 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, for that examination.
north-carolina.hold_extra: The full process — two examinations by different medical teams and a court hearing — can take up to 10 days, and the person is held for evaluation and treatment in the meantime.
north-carolina.initiators: Anyone with knowledge that the person needs immediate hospitalization — including a law enforcement officer — can transport the person directly to a facility for examination.
north-carolina.hearing: A court hearing must be held within 10 days.
north-carolina.link_label: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services — Involuntary Commitments

north-dakota.initiators: A peace officer, physician, psychiatrist, physician assistant, psychologist, advanced practice registered nurse, or mental health professional with reasonable cause can have the person taken into custody. A magistrate can also order it.
north-dakota.hearing: Within 72 hours of admission, the facility must release the person or file a petition with the court, and the magistrate must set a hearing for no later than 5 days after detention, not counting weekends and holidays. A lawyer is appointed if the person has none.
north-dakota.link_label: North Dakota Century Code Chapter 25-03.1 — Commitment Procedures, Sections 25-03.1-25 and

ohio.hold_extra: The person must be examined within 24 hours of arriving at the hospital. After that, the chief clinical officer can detain the person for up to 3 court days while the person agrees to stay voluntarily, a court affidavit is filed, or the person is discharged.
ohio.initiators: A psychiatrist, licensed physician, licensed clinical psychologist, certain certified psychiatric nurses or nurse practitioners, a health officer, a parole officer, a police officer, or a sheriff can take the person into custody and bring them to a hospital.
ohio.link_label: Ohio Revised Code Section 5122.10 — Emergency Hospitalization

oklahoma.hold: Up to 120 hours (5 days), not counting weekends and holidays.
oklahoma.initiators: Any person can seek emergency action, and a peace officer who reasonably believes the person needs treatment must take the person into protective custody.
oklahoma.hearing: If the person demands a jury trial, the court must hold it within 72 hours of the demand, not counting weekends and holidays.
oklahoma.link_label: Oklahoma Statutes Title 43A, Section 5-415 — Hearing; Records (Oklahoma State Courts Netwo

oregon.hold: Up to 5 judicial days — days the court is open, so weekends and court holidays do not count.
oregon.initiators: A peace officer can take the person into custody, a community mental health program director (or their designee) can direct it, and a licensed independent practitioner at the hospital can detain or admit the person for emergency care.
oregon.hearing: The person cannot be held beyond 5 judicial days without a hearing.
oregon.link_label: Oregon Revised Statutes Chapter 426, Sections 426.232 and 426.234 — Emergency Admission; D

pennsylvania.hold_extra: A physician must examine the person within 2 hours of arrival. If the facility wants to keep treating the person after 120 hours, it must file for extended treatment under Section 303 — up to 20 more days, with a hearing within 24 hours of filing.
pennsylvania.initiators: A physician can certify the need for emergency examination, a county administrator can issue a warrant, or a physician or other authorized person who personally saw the conduct can apply without a warrant. Police can bring the person in.
pennsylvania.hearing: For extended treatment under Section 303, an informal hearing must be held within 24 hours of the filing, and the court appoints a lawyer for the person.
pennsylvania.link_label: Pennsylvania Mental Health Procedures Act, Section 302 — Involuntary Emergency Examination

rhode-island.hold_extra: A psychiatrist must finish the preliminary examination and evaluation within 72 hours. If the psychiatrist finds the person is not a candidate for emergency certification, the person is discharged.
rhode-island.initiators: A physician (or a licensed psychiatric advanced practice nurse) who has examined the person can apply for emergency certification. If no physician is available, a qualified mental health professional or a police officer can apply.
rhode-island.hearing: To hold the person beyond the 10 days, the facility must file for civil court certification and have a hearing set under § 40.1-5-8.
rhode-island.link_label: Rhode Island General Laws Section 40.1-5-7 — Emergency Certification

south-carolina.hold: Up to 48 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
south-carolina.hold_extra: Within 48 hours of receiving the affidavit and physician’s certification, the probate court must review the evidence to decide whether there is probable cause to keep holding the person.
south-carolina.initiators: A person files a sworn affidavit, with a certification by at least one licensed physician who has examined the person, and the probate judge can order a law enforcement officer to take the person into custody.
south-carolina.hearing: A full hearing must be set within 15 days of admission, and the court appoints a lawyer if the person has none.
south-carolina.link_label: South Carolina Code of Laws, Title 44, Chapter 17, Section 44-17-410 — Emergency Admission

south-dakota.hold_extra: The person must be examined by a qualified mental health professional within 24 hours of being taken into custody, to decide whether custody should continue.
south-dakota.initiators: Any person 18 or older can complete a petition, verified by affidavit, saying the person is severely mentally ill and in immediate need of intervention. A peace officer can take the person into custody.
south-dakota.hearing: If custody continues, the person has the right to a hearing within 5 days of being taken into custody — 6 days if a weekend or holiday falls in that time, 7 days if both do.
south-dakota.link_label: South Dakota Department of Social Services, Division of Behavioral Health — Helping a Love

tennessee.hold: Emergency detention is for immediate examination. If a court finds probable cause, a judge can order the person held for up to 5 days, not counting weekends or holidays, while a probable cause hearing is arranged — and if no judge is available, the hospital can hold the person for no more than 24 hours.
tennessee.initiators: A law enforcement officer, a licensed physician, a licensed psychologist, or a designated qualified mental health professional can detain the person for immediate examination.
tennessee.hearing: At the probable cause hearing, the judge can order the person held for up to 15 days if they should be admitted.
tennessee.link_label: Tennessee General Assembly — Bill Information, summary of present law on emergency involun

texas.hold: Up to 48 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
texas.hold_extra: A preliminary examination must happen within that time, and the person must be released unless a court orders continued detention.
texas.initiators: A peace officer can take the person into custody without a warrant when there is a substantial risk of serious harm, or with a warrant issued by a magistrate. Any adult can also file a written application for emergency detention.
texas.hearing: If a judge signs an order of protective custody, a probable cause hearing must be held within 72 hours, and the full hearing on court-ordered treatment must be held within 14 days of the application being filed.
texas.link_label: Office of the Texas Governor — Mental Health Protections, Detaining a Mental Health Patien

utah.hold: Up to 72 hours after commitment, not counting Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays, unless a commitment application is filed or the person agrees to stay voluntarily.
utah.initiators: A responsible individual can apply in writing, with a certification by a licensed physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or designated examiner. A peace officer or mental health officer who sees the danger can also take the person into custody.
utah.link_label: Utah Legislature — Utah Code Section 26B-5-331, Temporary commitment — Requirements and pr

vermont.hold: A psychiatrist must examine the person within 24 hours of the first certification. If the psychiatrist issues a second certification, the person can be held for up to 72 more hours.
vermont.initiators: An interested party can apply with a certificate from a licensed physician. In an emergency, when a physician’s certificate cannot be obtained without serious delay, a law enforcement officer or mental health professional can ask a judge for a warrant for an immediate examination.
vermont.hearing: Once an application for involuntary treatment is filed, a probable cause hearing is held within 3 days.
vermont.link_label: Vermont Legislature — Vermont Statutes Title 18, Chapter 179, Sections 7504, 7505 and 7508

virginia.named: emergency custody order (ECO) and temporary detention order (TDO)
virginia.hold: An emergency custody order lasts up to 8 hours. A temporary detention order lasts up to 72 hours before a hearing — if the 72 hours end on a weekend, holiday, or day the court is closed, detention can run until the close of business on the next court day.
virginia.initiators: A magistrate issues the orders on the sworn petition of any responsible person or a treating physician, or on the magistrate’s own motion, after an evaluation by the local community services board or a certified evaluator. Law enforcement carries out the custody.
virginia.hearing: A commitment hearing must take place within the 72-hour temporary detention window.
virginia.link_label: Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services — Emergency Services f

washington.hold: Up to 72 hours for evaluation and treatment.
washington.initiators: A designated crisis responder can order detention, a peace officer can take the person into emergency custody, and a judge can order detention on the crisis responder’s request.
washington.hearing: If a petition is filed for 14 days of involuntary treatment, the court must hold a probable cause hearing within 120 hours of the start of detention.
washington.link_label: Washington State Health Care Authority — Designated crisis responders (DCR) and the Involu

west-virginia.hold: Up to 72 hours. A hospital physician can order the hold when no judge, mental hygiene commissioner, or magistrate can be reached right away.
west-virginia.initiators: Any adult can apply to the circuit court, a magistrate, or a mental hygiene commissioner for involuntary custody for examination. A hospital staff physician can also order a hold in a psychiatric emergency.
west-virginia.hearing: A probable cause hearing is held promptly — the order must say the hearing will be held right away, and it can be up to 24 hours after the person is taken into custody where the court has a standing order for that.
west-virginia.link_label: West Virginia Legislature — West Virginia Code Section 27-5-2, Involuntary custody for exa

wisconsin.hold: Up to 72 hours after the person is taken into custody, not counting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, unless a hearing is held.
wisconsin.initiators: A law enforcement officer can detain the person, and a court can order detention.
wisconsin.link_label: Wisconsin Legislature — Wisconsin Statutes Section 51.15, Emergency detention

wyoming.hold: Up to 72 hours, not counting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.
wyoming.initiators: A law enforcement officer or an examiner — a licensed psychiatrist, physician, advanced practice nurse, physician assistant, psychologist, professional counselor, addictions therapist, clinical social worker, or marriage and family therapist — can make the initial decision to detain the person.
wyoming.hearing: A preliminary hearing must be held within 72 hours of the emergency detention, and the person, their guardian, and their lawyer must be told about it.
wyoming.link_label: Wyoming Department of Health, Behavioral Health Division — Emergency Detention Process
